note: A 35-page policy paper with nine body figures, one landscape decision-matrix grid, four appendix captures and five uncaptioned plates. The body draws every figure in the same Excel engine - step charts for human capital, single-chip 'Frequency' bars for age and education - with in-plot titles standing in for captions and one drawn wage/People diagram as the only labelled exhibit. Captions print below in the body and above in the appendix, and the two runs number independently: 'Figure 1.' to 'Figure 9.' with a period, then 'Figure 1:' to 'Figure 3:' with a colon. From Figure 4 the running text is consistently one number ahead of the printed captions, and Figure 7's caption is the bare number with no description. The single grid is on the single landscape page and is measured as three bands of one table, with a repeated header and a title under the last band. Pages 33 to 35 have no text layer: they reprint body charts as full-page plates with no captions and no numbers.
rules: Two independent numbering runs share one paper: the body captions run 'Figure 1.' to 'Figure 9.' with a period, and the appendix restarts at 'Figure 1:' to 'Figure 3:' with a colon, so the same number names two different exhibits [caption.numbering].
Every body caption prints below its artwork and all three appendix captions print above their capture, so caption side follows the part of the paper, not the kind of exhibit [caption.position].

From Figure 4 onward the running text is one ahead of the printed captions: p13 cites 'Figure 5' for the caption 'Figure 4', p17 cites 'figure6 and 7' for the captions 'Figure 5' and 'Figure 6', p19 cites only '(see Figure)', and p21 cites 'Figure 10' for the caption 'Figure 9' [mention.style].
One caption names nothing at all: 'Figure 7.' is a number and a full stop, printed under a three-series plot that the following sentence never describes [caption.words].

Captions are short and nominal - 6 to 9 words in the body, 6 to 7 in the appendix, 4 for the matrix title - and not one names a unit, a variable or a condition, or states a conclusion [caption.units].

Five uncaptioned plates sit on the three pages that carry no text layer at all (pp33-35), each reprinting a body chart at full page width, so the appendix duplicates Figures 1, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 as plates that neither a caption nor a citation reaches [caption.verbatim].

The only grid in the paper sits on the only landscape page, and it is printed as three stacked bands that the region detector measured separately; the 'Values / Applications' header band repeats above both the weight strip and the main grid [table.orientation].

The matrix is drawn, not captured: cells are bounded by rules and filled with weight colours, there is no worksheet chrome, and the shading encodes the value rather than alternating rows [table.zebra].
Only the matrix's two score columns are decimal-aligned, and they are the only place raw spreadsheet precision reaches print (0.316111, 0.055555556) [table.decimal_aligned].
The matrix title is also its caption: 'Weighted Decison Matrix Model' prints under the last band, misspelled, with no label number of any kind [table.note_sentence].

Eight of the nine body figures come out of one Excel chart engine - five line charts, three of them staircases of the human-capital distribution, and three bar charts of age - sharing one frame, one gridline style and one font [geometry.family].

Only one body figure is a drawn diagram rather than a chart - the wage/People diagram of Figure 3 - and it is the only exhibit in the paper whose content is labelled regions rather than plotted values [geometry.data_labels].

Legends are used sparingly and always as a single chip: 'Frequency' to the right of the frame on the three bar charts, and one inside-frame legend below the plot on the three-series line chart [geometry.legend].
No exhibit in the paper is three-dimensional, none carries a colourbar, and the only colour scale is the conditional fill inside the decision matrix [geometry.colorbar].

In-plot titles stand in for captions: eight of the nine body charts repeat their year or population name inside the frame, and in one case title and caption disagree (Figure 5 is titled '+50 yrs' but captioned 2150) [geometry.printed_numbers].

Axis titling is inconsistent across one template: 'Human Capital Level' in Figures 1, 4 and 9 against 'Human Capital level' in Figure 8, and 'Age Group (5yrs)' against 'Age Group, 5 yrs' across the two halves of the p18 pair [geometry.shared_axes].

The appendix captures are screenshots, not drawings: worksheet gridlines, grey header cells, colour-filled inputs and empty cells print inside the measured region, and one dashboard is half covered by a solid black rectangle [geometry.data_labels].

One exhibit is notebook output rather than a figure: the Mathematica plot on p30 prints the code cells that drew it directly above the curve, and the plot has no axis titles, no legend and no caption [caption.verbatim].

Three charts clip or mislabel their own axes: Figure 9's curve rises into the frame corner and is cut off while its x axis runs on unlabelled, Figure 7 breaks its own two-decimal tick format by printing 0.1 over a 0.03-to-0.09 ladder, and the p34 plate has an x axis with no tick labels at all [geometry.printed_numbers].

The citation grammar splits three ways: a numbered reference ('can be found in Figure 1', 'as displayed in Figure 5'), a pure deictic ('pictured below', 'shown above:'), and one parenthetical '(see Figure)' with no number at all [mention.lead_pattern].

Body figures are cited on their own page; the appendix dashboard is cited on p14 and prints on p27, a thirteen-page lead announced by the words 'in Figure 1 of Appendix UL1' even though the appendix is printed under a different title [mention.lead_pages].

Exhibit size is uniform by part, not by importance: the nine body figures are all drawn in one fixed column at 0.07 to 0.11 of the page, while the five uncaptioned appendix plates take 0.16 each and say less than any captioned figure [place.area_frac].
